chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

I was seated in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he called for water, filled his palm with it, and washed his face with it. Then he filled his palm and washed his right hand with it. Then he filled his palm and washed his left hand with it. Then he wiped upon his head and his two feet, and said: 'This is the Wudu of the one who did not have a new event, meaning by it the transgression/excess in the Wudu.'

key_terms.التَّعَدِّي: Transgression or excess (going beyond the prescribed limits)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method for performing Wudu according to the Imams when not in a state of major impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the Sunnah method of Wudu by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the specific sequence of washing the face, hands, and wiping the head and feet. The phrase 'not exceeding limits' (al-ta'tid) refers to the scholarly principle of ensuring each body part is washed three times, a practice widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence as the normative standard for ritual purity. It serves as a primary textual basis for the detailed fiqh of ablution, distinguishing it from the more comprehensive Ghusl required for major impurity.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,

‘I was seated in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws called for the water. Then heasws filled hisasws palm with it and impacted hisasws face with it. Then heasws filled hisasws palm and impacted hisasws right hand with it. Then heasws filled his palm and impacted hisasws left hand with it. Then heasws wiped upon hisasws head and his feet and said: ‘This is an Ablution (Wudhu) of the one who does not have a newly occurring event, meaning by it the transgression regarding the Ablution (Wudhu)’ (innovation).
en.sarwar: 8. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) asked for water. He then filled up his hand with water and allowed it to flow over all of his face. He then filled the palm of his hand with water and washed therewith his right hand. He then filled the palm of his right hand with water, washed therewith his left hand and thereafter wiped his head and feet saying, This is a Wudu 5 of one who does not invent anything in it, meaning thereby transgression against the limits of Wudu”
